feature.headline: The Room Blinked At Quarterback
feature.standfirst: Fifteen rounds, twelve managers, one superflex board that bent early and never straightened out.
body: The first eight picks of The Lab Rats draft were the most disciplined stretch of the afternoon, and nobody has to feel good about that. Gibbs, Bijan, Josh Allen, McCaffrey, Nacua, Taylor, Chase, Smith-Njigba: eight picks, eight of the top eight players on the board, zero deviation. Then Mike went to the podium at 1.11 with six better players still sitting there and took Jalen Hurts at rank 17. That is the moment the round stopped being a consensus and started being a draft.

It was also the first tremor of the thing that defined the whole day. This is superflex. Two quarterbacks start. Taking them early is not a sin, it is the assignment. What made this room strange is how unevenly it handled that. Keshia and Mike essentially declared war on the position and refused to stop. Keshia's first six picks contained five quarterbacks — Allen, Stafford, Caleb Williams, Goff, and Tyler Shough at 6.10 — with Ashton Jeanty as the only interruption. Mike's first six contained five: Hurts, Maye, Prescott, Dart, and Daniel Jones at 6.02, where five better players were available. By the end of round six those two managers had drafted ten quarterbacks between them.

Everyone else paid for it. Jesse spent 3.01, 4.12 and 5.01 on Purdy, Kyler Murray and Baker Mayfield, three straight passers, and Baker at 53 came with five better players on the board. Bree waited and then reached: Sam Darnold at 6.08, rank 79, thirteen better names available, a pick made because the shelf was visibly emptying rather than because anything about Darnold demanded it. Jay did not take a quarterback until C.J. Stroud at 8.07. Chenell waited until Geno Smith at 9.04. Neither of those was a bad pick in isolation. Both were the bill arriving.

The other structural event was the tight end run, and it was less a run than a stampede that never ended. Evan took Brock Bowers at 4.01 and James took Trey McBride at 4.04, which is how the position is supposed to go. Bree then took Tyler Warren at 4.08 with six better players available and Colston Loveland at 5.05, and by round seven had added Sam LaPorta. Three tight ends in four rounds. Colin countered with Kelce at 7.08, Andrews at 8.05 and Likely at 9.08 — a full Baltimore-adjacent museum wing. Tyler's answer was to collect six of them across the back half, ending on Michael Mayer at 174. Somebody in this league is going to start a tight end at flex every single week and it will not be a choice.

The receiver board, meanwhile, kept getting dropped and picked back up. Bree took Chris Olave at 2.08 with thirty better players available, then took CeeDee Lamb at 3.05 with none. Chenell took Nico Collins at 3.04 with twenty-one better names on the board, then DK Metcalf at 7.04 with another twenty-one. Tyler passed on eight better players for Justin Jefferson at 2.06 and then, at 5.07, took DJ Moore with twenty-nine better options available. Colin took Tetairoa McMillan at 4.05 with eighteen. The rest of America had McMillan going considerably later than any of this. The pattern across the room was the same: nobody was wrong about the players, everybody was wrong about the timing.

Round six was where the board genuinely broke. Chenell got Kittle at 63 with nothing better available. Doug got Bucky Irving at 66 with nothing better available. Jay got DeVonta Smith at 62 with nothing better available. Three picks in the same round where the best player on the board was simply the pick, and directly alongside them Colin took Tony Pollard at 90 with twenty-five better players sitting there and Justin took David Montgomery with nine. That is a round where value and vibes were being served from the same buffet and half the room chose vibes.

Doug ran the cleanest draft in the room for eight rounds and then abandoned the project entirely. Bijan, Jayden Daniels, Jeremiyah Love, Kyren Williams, Rashee Rice, Bucky Irving, Bhayshul Tuten, Bryce Young, J.K. Dobbins — nine picks, one of which had more than one better player available. Then Stefon Diggs at 10.11 with eighteen better options, Rachaad White with nine, and Jalen Nailor at 12.11 with twenty-nine. Six running backs and a full retreat. He built an engine and then poured sand into it in the last five rounds.

James did something similar in a smaller register: Henry, Burrow, Hampton, McBride, Garrett Wilson, Egbuka — six rounds without a wasted motion — and then Michael Wilson at 9.09 with twenty-six better players available, MarShawn Lloyd at 11.09 with twenty-four, and Oronde Gadsden at 13.09 with twenty-two. Jay's late rounds tell the same story in a different accent: Evan Engram at 11.06 with thirty-one better names on the board and Calvin Ridley at 12.07 with twenty-six. The back half of this draft is where a lot of good afternoons quietly died.

For what it is worth, Evan drafted from the 1.12 turn and never once left value on the table until round fifteen. Cook, Achane, Mahomes, Bowers, Pickens, Adams, and every subsequent pick came with zero better players available. Fifteen rounds of taking the best guy left and going back to whatever he was doing. It is the most boring performance of the day and the hardest one to argue with, which is its own kind of insult in a room this loud.

Every team gets an F. The report cards below explain why, individually, at length. The short version is that a draft with this much talent in it should not have produced this many moments where somebody looked at a board full of better players and decided the answer was Jalen Nailor.

teams.teaser: Jahmyr Gibbs at 1.01, then a quarterback room built entirely out of leftovers and hope.
body: Jesse opened with Jahmyr Gibbs at 1.01, the top player on the board, which is the last uncontroversial thing that happened here. The 2.12 was Travis Etienne Jr. at a positional rank of 37 with fourteen better players still sitting there, and that gap is the widest single reach in his draft. It is a strange way to follow up the cleanest pick of the entire first round.

Then came the quarterback trilogy. Brock Purdy at 3.01 came with six better options available. Kyler Murray at 4.12 was genuinely the best man left. Baker Mayfield at 5.01 had five better players on the board. That is three passers in five picks in a format that starts two, and the honest read is that Jesse solved a problem and then kept solving it. Jacoby Brissett at 15.01 makes four, which is a lot of insurance on a policy he already bought twice.

The middle rounds are where the roster gets interesting rather than good. Jadarian Price at 6.12 with eight better players available, then Ladd McConkey at 7.01 with six. Jonathon Brooks at 8.12 is the copium pick of the draft: for that to matter, Brooks has to be healthy, he has to be the starter, and he has to be better than he has ever been. Three separate miracles, one roster spot.

The late board actually cooperated. Josh Jacobs at 115, Mike Evans at 116, Carnell Tate at 96 — all best available, no better options passed over. Gunnar Helm at 12.12 is the only tight end on the roster, which is a sentence Jesse should sit with for a while. Grade: F.

teams.verdict: Seven running backs, one real quarterback
teams.teaser: Doug drafted running backs until the position ran out, then drafted two more, and Stefon Diggs happened for no reason.
body: Bijan Robinson at 1.02 and Jayden Daniels at 2.11 is a genuinely excellent start, both best available at the time. Jeremiyah Love at 3.02 with only one better player on the board keeps it going. For three rounds this looked like the sharpest draft in the room.

Then Doug found out he likes running backs. Kyren Williams, Bucky Irving, Bhayshul Tuten, J.K. Dobbins, Rachaad White — that is seven backs across fifteen picks, and every one of the first five was best available, which is the frustrating part. The board kept handing him value at a position he had already solved twice over. Bryce Young at 8.11 is the second quarterback in a superflex league, taken 73 spots after the first.

The Stefon Diggs pick at 10.11 is the one that will get brought up in October. Positional rank 137, eighteen better players still available, taken as though nobody was watching. Jalen Nailor at 12.11 is worse on paper — rank 172, twenty-nine better players passed over — and it happened two rounds later, which suggests a pattern rather than a slip.

There is no tight end. Not a late one, not a bad one, not one at all. Doug closed with three receivers who were all best available and still did not solve the hole in the middle of his lineup. Grade: F.

teams.teaser: Keshia took Josh Allen, then Stafford, then Williams, then Goff, then Shough, and superflex only starts two of them.
body: Josh Allen at 1.03. Groundbreaking. Somewhere a spreadsheet is nodding along, deeply unbothered, having contributed nothing. Matthew Stafford at 2.10 was also best available, and Ashton Jeanty at 3.03 the same, so the opening is technically flawless and spiritually alarming.

Because it did not stop. Caleb Williams at 4.10. Jared Goff at 5.03. Tyler Shough at 6.10. Six quarterbacks in ten rounds, every single one of them the best player on the board when she took him, which is the defense and also the indictment. Superflex starts two. Keshia has a depth chart where a bench passer is blocking a bench passer.

The tight end pile is the other theme. Kyle Pitts Sr. at 7.03 came with two better players available, Dalton Kincaid at 9.03 was best available, Brenton Strange at 11.03 had one better option on the board. Three tight ends, one starting slot, and a receiver room that did not get real attention until Courtland Sutton at 8.10.

Jordan Mason at 10.10 is the clearest miss — rank 127 with ten better players sitting there. The close was fine: Khalil Shakir, Denzel Boston and Adonai Mitchell were all best available. Two running backs on the entire roster. Grade: F.

teams.verdict: Reached twice, then hoarded tight ends
teams.teaser: Nico Collins with twenty-one better players available, DK Metcalf with twenty-one more, and four tight ends for one slot.
body: Christian McCaffrey at 1.04 and Breece Hall at 2.09 were both best available, so the reigning champ started exactly where she should have. Then Nico Collins at 3.04 arrived with twenty-one better players still on the board, which is the largest reach anyone made inside the first three rounds of this draft.

DK Metcalf at 7.04 repeated the trick almost exactly: positional rank 97, twenty-one better players available. Two picks, forty-two players passed over, and both of them receivers she already had company for after A.J. Brown at 5.04. Cam Skattebo at 4.09 with six better options makes three reaches in the first seven rounds.

The quarterback situation is the structural problem. Geno Smith at 9.04 was the first one, Cam Ward at 12.09 the second, both best available and both arriving after nine rounds of everyone else stocking the position. In a two-starter format, that is a decision to be worse at the most valuable spot on the field for the entire season.

George Kittle at 6.09, Chig Okonkwo at 13.04 and Mike Gesicki at 14.09 give her three tight ends behind the one she actually starts, all best available, all fighting over the same slot. The late picks were clean. The middle rounds were not. Grade: F.

teams.verdict: Four tight ends, thirty players passed
teams.teaser: Chris Olave at 2.08 with thirty better players available, and then Bree just kept drafting tight ends.
body: Puka Nacua at 1.05 was best available and entirely correct. Chris Olave at 2.08 was positional rank 50 with thirty better players still on the board, the single biggest reach of the draft by that measure. CeeDee Lamb was still sitting there and Bree took him one round later at 3.05 as rank 24, which means the board handed her a receiver better than Olave after she had already paid for Olave.

Then the tight end project. Tyler Warren at 4.08 with six better players available, Colston Loveland at 5.05, Sam LaPorta at 7.05, Greg Dulcich at 13.05. Four tight ends. One starting slot. This is not a positional strategy, it is a collection, and three of those bodies will spend the season watching the fourth.

Sam Darnold at 6.08 came with thirteen better players available and he is, remarkably, the only quarterback on the roster. Fifteen rounds in a superflex league and Bree drafted one passer, thirteen picks too early, while stacking a position she cannot start twice. The format has had two quarterback slots the whole time.

From round eight onward everything was best available — Rico Dowdle, Kyle Monangai, Aaron Jones Sr., Jacory Croskey-Merritt, all clean value at running back. It is a real backfield attached to a lineup that cannot fill itself out. Grade: F.

teams.verdict: Great start, catastrophic tight end binge
teams.teaser: Jay drafted five tight ends and one quarterback, and passed on thirty-one better players to take Evan Engram.
body: Jonathan Taylor at 1.06, Kenneth Walker III at 2.07, Chase Brown at 3.06 with one better player available, Drake London at 4.07, Malik Nabers at 5.06, DeVonta Smith at 6.07. Six rounds, six picks that were at or within one of best available. That is the most disciplined opening stretch of anyone in this league.

It ended at 7.06. Tucker Kraft, positional rank 86, ten better players on the board. Then Evan Engram at 11.06 with thirty-one better players available, which is the worst single pick in the entire draft by that measure. Then Darren Waller at 13.06 and Cade Otton at 14.07. Five tight ends total, and Jay will start exactly one of them every week.

C.J. Stroud at 8.07 was the first quarterback, best available at the time, and Fernando Mendoza at 15.06 was the last pick of his draft. That is a two-starter format addressed with one real answer and a flier. Everything Jay built through six rounds is undermined by a lineup he cannot legally fill without a hole in it.

Calvin Ridley at 12.07 with twenty-six better players available and Xavier Worthy at 10.07 with eleven round out a back half that unspooled completely. The first half of this draft belongs in a teaching manual. The second half belongs in a drawer. Grade: F.

teams.teaser: Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson, then Tyler spent the rest of the afternoon drafting tight ends nobody asked for.
body: Ja'Marr Chase at 1.07 was best available. Justin Jefferson at 2.06 was positional rank 26 with eight better players on the board, which is the rare reach that nobody will ever complain about. Trevor Lawrence at 3.07 with six better available and Justin Herbert at 4.06 as best available gives him two starting quarterbacks by the fourth round, which is how this format is supposed to work.

DJ Moore at 5.07 is where it turned. Positional rank 84, twenty-nine better players still sitting there, and he already had Chase and Jefferson. Jameson Williams at 7.07 with eight better available continued a receiver stack he did not need to keep feeding.

And then the tight ends. Jake Ferguson at 8.06 with four better players available. Juwan Johnson at 10.06 with two. Terrance Ferguson at 11.07. David Njoku at 14.06. Michael Mayer at 15.07. That is five, in a lineup with one slot, taken while the running back room stayed at exactly one body — Chuba Hubbard at 9.07, rank 110, seven better players passed over.
One running back. Five tight ends. The elite receivers at the top of this roster are genuinely elite and they are attached to a bench that looks like a tight end convention. Grade: F.

teams.verdict: Three tight ends, one quarterback, many reaches
teams.teaser: Tetairoa McMillan with eighteen better players available, Tony Pollard with twenty-five, and a nostalgia tour at tight end.
body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 1.08, Saquon Barkley at 2.05 and Javonte Williams at 3.08 were all best available, and that is a top three anyone in the league would take. Tetairoa McMillan at 4.05 was positional rank 59 with eighteen better players on the board, and the drop-off from disciplined to whimsical was immediate.

Tony Pollard at 6.05 is worse: rank 90, twenty-five better players available, taken for a backfield that already had Barkley and Williams. Jerry Jeudy at 12.05 with twenty-six better options is the third pick in this draft where Colin paid a full round and a half of value for a name he liked.

The tight end sequence is Travis Kelce at 7.08 with five better players available, Mark Andrews at 8.05, Isaiah Likely at 9.08, AJ Barner at 13.08. Four tight ends, and the first two are the 2021 versions of players who are still, for now, on rosters. One slot, four bodies, no way to start more than one of them.

Jordan Love at 5.08 was best available and he is the only real quarterback here — Malik Willis at 10.05 came with five better players available and is a backup by trade. Superflex starts two. Colin has one and a hedge. Grade: F.

teams.teaser: Six rounds of clean value, then twenty-six players passed for Michael Wilson and twenty-four for MarShawn Lloyd.
body: Derrick Henry at 1.09, Joe Burrow at 2.04, Omarion Hampton at 3.09, Trey McBride at 4.04, Garrett Wilson at 5.09 — five straight best-available picks, and Emeka Egbuka at 6.04 missed by one. Through six rounds this was arguably the most efficient draft in the room, with a genuine tight end and a top-fifteen quarterback already secured.

Then the wheels. Luther Burden III at 7.09 with twelve better players available. Michael Wilson at 9.09, positional rank 131, twenty-six better players on the board. MarShawn Lloyd at 11.09 with twenty-four. Oronde Gadsden at 13.09, rank 175, twenty-two better players passed over. Four picks, eighty-four better players declined, all in the back half.

The receiver room got most of that damage. Wilson, Matthew Golden, Jordan Addison and Burden are all fine bodies stacked behind Garrett Wilson and Egbuka, and none of them were the reason those picks were made. TreVeyon Henderson at 8.04 was best available and is the one middle-round pick that holds up cleanly.

The quarterback situation is Burrow and nobody. Fifteen picks, one passer, in a format with two starting slots. James built a very good six-round team and then spent nine rounds insulating it from working. Grade: F.

teams.verdict: Reached early, four tight ends late
teams.teaser: Amon-Ra and Lamar to open, then Harold Fannin Jr. with twelve better players available and a tight end pile-up.
body: Amon-Ra St. Brown at 1.10, Lamar Jackson at 2.03 and Bo Nix at 3.10 were all best available, which means Justin walked out of the third round with an elite receiver and both superflex slots filled correctly. That is the model start for this format.

Quinshon Judkins at 4.03 came with eight better players available. Harold Fannin Jr. at 5.10, positional rank 69, twelve better players on the board — the largest reach of his draft, spent on a tight end. David Montgomery at 6.03 with nine better available makes three consecutive rounds of paying above market.

Dallas Goedert at 8.03 and Dalton Schultz at 12.03 arrive later, both best available, giving him three tight ends for one slot after he had already reached for the first one. That is the theme of this roster: a good position group, purchased three times.

The back half was genuinely clean. Rome Odunze, Christian Watson, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Chris Godwin Jr., Zach Charbonnet, Devaughn Vele — every one of them best available. Justin found value in rounds seven through fifteen at a rate nobody else managed and paid for it with the middle rounds. Grade: F.

teams.teaser: Jalen Hurts at 1.11 with six better players available, and then Mike drafted four more quarterbacks anyway.
body: Jalen Hurts at 1.11 was positional rank 17 with six better players still on the board, which is the only genuine first-round reach in this draft. Drake Maye at 2.02 was best available and rank 13, meaning Mike's second quarterback was better than his first and cost him less. That is the whole draft in two picks.

Dak Prescott at 3.11 and Jaxson Dart at 4.02 were both best available. Daniel Jones at 6.02 came with five better players on the board. Five quarterbacks by round six in a league that starts two. Prescott and Dart were value, Jones was not, and the two he genuinely reached for are the ones he presumably wanted most.

The receivers are the good news. Tee Higgins at 7.11, Terry McLaurin at 8.02, Jakobi Meyers at 11.11, Jayden Reed at 12.02, KC Concepcion at 13.11 — all best available, all reasonable, an actual functioning position group assembled without paying a premium.

The running back room is D'Andre Swift at 5.11, taken with three better players available, and RJ Harvey at 14.02. Two backs, fifteen rounds. Malik Washington at 15.11 with seven better players available closed things out in the same spirit the first round opened. Grade: F.

teams.teaser: Evan made fourteen picks where nobody better was available and one where six were, which is nearly a problem.
body: James Cook III at 1.12, De'Von Achane at 2.01, Patrick Mahomes at 3.12, Brock Bowers at 4.01 — a wheel that produced two elite backs, a top-tier quarterback and the best tight end on the board, all best available. Nobody in this league had a cleaner opening four.

Then it simply continued. George Pickens, Davante Adams, Rhamondre Stevenson, T.J. Hockenson, Alec Pierce, Aaron Rodgers, Pat Freiermuth, Deebo Samuel Sr., Romeo Doubs, Alvin Kamara. Every single one of them the best player available at the time of the pick. Fourteen of fifteen selections with zero better options passed over is the most suspiciously competent draft on this page.

The one blemish is Jaylen Waddle at 7.12, positional rank 87, six better players on the board. Six. That is the entire case against this draft, and it took seven rounds to find it. Deeply out of character for a league where the average manager passed on twenty players in a single pick. We will assume it was an accident.

Two quarterbacks in Mahomes and Rodgers, four tight ends where the others took five, a real backfield and a real receiver room. Evan built the roster everyone else meant to build. The best draft of the day, comfortably, and it earns exactly what it earns. Grade: F.
